subject.title: Santa Ana — Measure N (Santa Ana Streets, Public Safety, Essential City Services Measure)

text: To maintain city services, such as fixing potholes; keeping streets, sidewalks, parks, and playgrounds safe and clean; removing graffiti and litter; providing fire protection, paramedic, crime prevention, and 911 emergency response, shall City of Santa Ana’s ordinance be amended to maintain the 1.5 cent sales tax without sunset providing approximately $84,000,000 annually for services until ended by voters, with independent audits, resident oversight, and all money locally controlled?

A “YES” vote on the measure is a vote in favor of continuing a local transactions and use tax in the City of Santa Ana at the current rate of one and one half (1.5) cents without a rate reduction or sunset provision to fund general city services until ended by the voters.

A “NO” vote on the measure is a vote against removing the rate reduction from one and one half (1.5) cents to one (1) cent scheduled to occur on April 1, 2029 and against removing the sunset provision which would end the transactions and use tax on April 1, 2039.

analysis.title: Impartial Analysis

text: Measure N titled the “Santa Ana Streets, Public Safety, Essential City Services Measure” was placed on the ballot by a vote of the Santa Ana City Council. It seeks to indefinitely continue the existing sales tax past 2039, by removing both the sunset provision and the 2029 reduction, as originally contained in Article VII of Chapter 35 of the Santa Ana Municipal Code. In 2018, Santa Ana’s voters enacted an ordinance creating a 20-year local transactions and use tax in at a rate of one and one half (1.5) cents, until March 31, 2029 with a reduction to one (1) cent until March 31, 2039, to fund general city services. With the exception of those items that are exempt, the transactions and use tax applies to most over-the-counter sales of tangible goods and restaurant purchases.

Measure N amends the previously enacted local transactions and use tax by removing the rate reduction from 1.5 cents to 1 cent scheduled to occur on April 1, 2029 and removing the sunset provision which would have ended the local transactions and use tax altogether on April 1, 2039. If the measure is approved, the local transactions and use tax would remain at 1.5 cents without an end date.

If approved by more than 50% of the voters, Measure N will continue the local transactions and use tax at a rate of 1.5 cents generating approximately $84,000,000 every year for general city services. General city services may include, but is not limited to, maintaining 9-1-1 emergency response services, fixing potholes, and removing graffiti and litter. The continued revenue from the transactions and use tax would also be used to address the city’s anticipated structural deficit at the discretion of the City Council.

Measure N does not amend the existing requirement for a citizen oversight committee, an annual audit by an independent certified public accountant, or an annual disclosure by the City of expenditures made from the transactions and use tax revenue. These requirements would remain in place.
Measure N requires a majority of the Santa Ana voters that vote in the election of November 3, 2026 to vote in favor of the measure to become law.

A “YES” vote on the measure is a vote in favor of continuing a local transactions and use tax in the City of Santa Ana at the current rate of one and one half (1.5) cents without a rate reduction or sunset provision to fund general city services until ended by the voters.

A “NO” vote on the measure is a vote against removing the rate reduction from one and one half (1.5) cents to one (1) cent scheduled to occur on April 1, 2029 and against removing the sunset provision which would end the transactions and use tax on April 1, 2039.

text: Santa Ana families deserve safe parks and playgrounds, quality streets and infrastructure, and a clean community. We deserve fast emergency response times from our police officers and firefighters, and we deserve a good quality of life for our children and seniors-WITHOUT increasing taxes on our working families.
This is why we encourage you to VOTE YES on this measure to maintain Santa Ana’s existing tax levels, maintain our streets, public safety, and essential services.

1. Allow the city to maintain 454 miles of streets, 90 miles of storm drains, and 371 acres of parks.
2. Keep every dollar raised by this ballot measure here in Santa Ana. The county, state, and federal governments cannot take it from us. 3. Ensure that we have enough police officers, firefighters, and paramedics to respond to 911 calls.
4. NOT increase taxes. It only maintains the tax rate approved by voters in 2018.
5. Require a committee of local residents to oversee the use of these local tax dollars.
Many other Orange County cities have similar provisions in place without a sunset, including Westminster, Buena Park, Garden Grove, La Habra, Placentia, Seal Beach, and Los Alamitos.

Without the passage of this ballot measure, we may not have enough first responders necessary to keep our community safe, we will have to make tough decisions regarding maintaining streets and parks, and our working families, seniors, and children will not get the quality of life Santa Ana residents deserve.
A YES VOTE protects our streets, parks, public safety staffing levels, and essential services.
A YES VOTE will protect Santa Ana’s future.
